# Harleen Kaur — enterprise AI engineering

> Open-source work in LLM model routing, agent governance, containment testing, and application evaluation. This portfolio links runnable examples and evidence with explicit limitations.

The featured customer-summary workflow connects AxonLLM, Ostiari, and Escape Lab through a deterministic synthetic fixture. Practical Eval Lab supplies separate application-evaluation examples. The public material supports inspection of engineering work; it does not establish production adoption, business savings, executive scope, or general safety certification.

## Start here
- [Portfolio in Markdown](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/index.md): The four projects, their relationship, and runnable entry points.
- [Engineering case study](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/case-study.md): The customer-summary boundary, paired results, exact source references, and limitations.
- [Engineering decisions](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/decisions.md): Product boundaries, governance choices, and evidence practices.
- [Run the integration](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/run-example.md): Locked installation and reproduction commands.
- [Engineering blog](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/): Articles on AI workloads, design decisions, and evaluation evidence.
- [Renewal Studio series](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/renewal-studio.html): All nine parts, with 28 interactive workflows covering software and API contract renewals, retention, agents, finance and the operational pilot path.
- [Renewal Studio, Part 1: The Standard Renewal, End to End](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/renewal-studio-standard-renewal.html): The buyer accepts. Billing succeeds. Access fails. Explore four interactive workflows showing how a standard renewal qualifies, records consent, activates and recovers.
- [Renewal Studio, Part 2: When the Standard Path Ends](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/renewal-studio-exceptions.html): A shorter term and a new clause turn one renewal into several decisions. Explore commercial routing, versioned approvals and strategic procurement.
- [Renewal Studio, Part 3: Renewing a Commitment When Usage Changes](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/renewal-studio-consumption.html): A precise shortfall projection can still rest on bad data. Follow reconciled usage through intervention, evidence review and commitment rightsizing.
- [Renewal Studio, Part 4: Retention Beyond the Renewal Date](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/renewal-studio-retention.html): Lower spend can mean better efficiency. Follow customer value, explicit cancellation decisions and verified reactivation across three interactive workflows.
- [Renewal Studio, Part 5: The Work After the Sale](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/renewal-studio-post-sale.html): The agreement is active, but the integration is blocked. Connect post-sale milestones, partner evidence and customer replies to owned outcomes.
- [Renewal Studio, Part 6: Follow the Money](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/renewal-studio-finance.html): A payment succeeds but its acknowledgement disappears. Explore reservations, reconciliation, refunds and exact-cent service allocation.
- [Renewal Studio, Part 7: Let Agents Work Within a Boundary](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/renewal-studio-agents.html): An agent can propose a plan without gaining permission to accept for the buyer. Explore provider boundaries, durable scheduling and execution-based evaluations.
- [Renewal Studio, Part 8: Forecast the Business from the Work](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/renewal-studio-forecasting.html): Preserve what the business believed last week. Explore operational forecasts, synthetic model evaluation and multi-cycle portfolio experiments.
- [Renewal Studio, Part 9: From Demonstration to an Operational System](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/renewal-studio-operations.html): Connect the hosted AWS demo to its source, identity and recovery boundaries, then define the evidence a narrowly scoped real pilot would need.
- [Improving Agents Starts with Verifying the Work](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/improving-agents-starts-with-verifying-the-work.html): I compared reported completion with verified outputs in a live AutoHelix experiment. Inspect the results, scripted cheating controls, and limits of editing the improvement strategy.
- [Your AI remembers you. Can it remember a lie?](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/your-ai-remembers-you-can-it-remember-a-lie.html): Follow a false approval across sessions, inspect 40 synthetic memory-authority episodes, and see why provenance and current permission need separate checks.
- [Testing subscription abuse at the action boundary](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/testing-subscription-abuse-at-the-action-boundary.html): A synthetic subscription workflow compares permissions, business invariants, and deny-all controls, with recorded effects, explicit completion limits, and replayable evidence.
- [Designing an Evidence Trail for Agent Actions](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/designing-an-evidence-trail-for-agent-actions.html): I trace one synthetic agent action from its request to its observed effect, then examine what event hashes, snapshots, and replay can establish—and what needs additional verification.
- [When rules beat decision models](https://hk-775.github.io/hk-775/blog/when-rules-beat-decision-models.html): I replaced a label-matching diagnostic with an executable support workflow. On 144 synthetic test episodes, the rules baseline outperformed the tested zero-shot model configurations.
